title.value: CACHE (Critical Assessment of Computational Hit-finding Experiments): A public–private partnership benchmarking initiative to enable the development of computational methods for hit-finding
title.justification: The title is clearly stated in the introduction and throughout the document as: 'CACHE (Critical Assessment of Computational Hit-finding Experiments): A public–private partnership benchmarking initiative to enable the development of computational methods for hit-finding'.
title.quote: CACHE (Critical Assessment of Computational Hit-finding Experiments): A public-private partnership benchmarking initiative to enable the development of computational methods for hit-finding.

analysis.description: The paper introduces CACHE, a public-private partnership project designed to benchmark computational methods for identifying small-molecule binders to proteins. This initiative aims to improve hit-finding algorithms through cycles of prediction and experimental testing, and emphasizes an open-access approach to data sharing without intellectual property restrictions.

type.justification: The paper describes empirical efforts in benchmarking and improving computational methods for hit-finding through experimental validation of predictions.
type.quote: ...a public benchmarking project to compare and improve small-molecule hit-finding algorithms through cycles of prediction and experimental testing.

name.justification: The paper focuses on computational methods in chemistry, specifically related to predicting molecular binders in drug discovery.
name.quote: One aspirational goal of computational chemistry is to predict potent and drug-like binders for any protein... in this Roadmap, we describe the launch of Critical Assessment of Computational Hit-finding Experiments (CACHE)...

name.justification: The paper targets the use of computational methods to discover small-molecule binders for drug discovery.
name.quote: CACHE will benchmark computational approaches for the identification of a small molecule that binds a targeted protein with high enough affinity and suitable physiochemical properties to qualify as a credible starting point for a drug discovery project.

name.justification: The paper mentions the use of machine learning approaches in improving computational hit-finding methods.
name.quote: Prompted by recent developments and interest in computational methods, including deep learning, as well as the challenges in identifying the best performing methods...

name.justification: ZINC20 is mentioned as part of the virtual library for testing predictions, indicating its role as a dataset.
name.quote: A combination of Enamine REAL (now providing 21 billion make-on-demand compounds) and ZINC20 (ref. ^{19} ) (containing over 750 million purchasable compounds) might comprise the core of this library.
